settings.phone_desc: Open TERMNEST in your phone's browser, through a VPN (Tailscale or your company VPN) or an SSH tunnel to the machine that runs it. That machine should be always on, such as a server; do not expose it to the Internet. Once you are in, choose “Install as an app” in Settings on the phone to get an icon on the home screen.

guide.title: Use TERMNEST on your phone
guide.lead: Choose how to connect. Whichever you pick, the machine that runs TERMNEST must stay on.
guide.open_url: Then open this address in your phone’s browser:
guide.ssh.title: Before you start (SSH methods)
guide.ssh.body: You need SSH access to the machine that runs TERMNEST: its address, a user name, and a password or key. TERMNEST listens only on 127.0.0.1:7681; the SSH app carries that port to your phone.
guide.ssh.mac: Mac: System Settings → General → Sharing → turn on Remote Login.
guide.ssh.linux: Linux: install and start the SSH server (sudo apt install openssh-server).
guide.tailscale.name: Tailscale
guide.tailscale.blurb: The easiest option. A private network between your devices; nothing is exposed to the Internet.
guide.tailscale.1.t: Install Tailscale on the machine that runs TERMNEST
guide.tailscale.1.d: Create a free account at tailscale.com and sign in. On Linux, run:
guide.tailscale.1.n: On macOS or Windows, download the app from tailscale.com/download instead.
guide.tailscale.2.t: Publish TERMNEST inside your private network
guide.tailscale.2.d: This creates a private https address that only your own devices can open:
guide.tailscale.2.n: Copy the address it prints, for example https://my-machine.my-tailnet.ts.net. If asked, enable MagicDNS and HTTPS in the Tailscale admin console.
guide.tailscale.3.d: Without this, the page answers “403”. Set the host name (without https://) before TERMNEST starts:
guide.tailscale.3.n: For a systemd service, add it as Environment= in the service, then restart it.
guide.tailscale.4.d: Get Tailscale from the App Store or Google Play, sign in with the same account and switch it on.
guide.tailscale.5.t: Open the address in your browser
guide.tailscale.5.d: Open the address from step 2 in Safari or Chrome and sign in with your TERMNEST password.
guide.tailscale.6.t: Add it to your home screen
guide.tailscale.6.d: iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen. Android: ⋮ menu → Install app.
guide.tailscale.tip: Never use “tailscale funnel”: it would expose TERMNEST to the whole Internet.
guide.termius.name: Termius
guide.termius.blurb: A polished SSH app with built-in port forwarding. No extra software on the server.
guide.termius.1.t: Add your machine as a host
guide.termius.1.d: Open Termius → Hosts → + → New Host. Enter the address, user name and password or key, then save.
guide.termius.2.d: Open Port Forwarding → + → New Rule, and fill in:
guide.termius.3.d: Switch the rule on. Termius shows it as connected.
guide.termius.4.n: Keep Termius open. An iPhone may pause the tunnel while the app is in the background.
guide.termux.name: Termux
guide.termux.blurb: Android only. A real terminal on your phone; the tunnel is one command.
guide.termux.1.d: Get Termux from F-Droid. The Google Play version is outdated.
guide.termux.3.d: Replace user and machine-address, enter the password when asked, and leave Termux running:
guide.termux.4.d: Pull down the Termux notification and tap “Acquire wakelock”, so Android does not stop the tunnel.
guide.connectbot.name: ConnectBot
guide.connectbot.blurb: Android only. A light, free SSH app with port forwards built in.
guide.connectbot.1.d: Open ConnectBot → +, enter user@machine-address, connect once and accept the host key.
guide.connectbot.2.d: Long-press the host → Edit port forwards → +, then fill in:
guide.connectbot.3.d: Tap the host to connect and keep the session open.
guide.other.name: Other SSH app
guide.other.blurb: JuiceSSH, Blink Shell, Prompt… any app that supports local port forwarding.
guide.other.1.d: Look for “Port forwarding”, “Tunnels” or “Local forward” in the app.
guide.other.2.d: Use these values. The equivalent command is:
guide.other.tip: Bind the local port to 127.0.0.1 only, never to 0.0.0.0.
guide.help.title: Troubleshooting
guide.help.403.d: The address is not allowed. With Tailscale, set TW_ALLOWED_HOSTS (step 3). With SSH, open exactly localhost or 127.0.0.1.
guide.help.conn.d: Check that the machine is on, TERMNEST is running, and the VPN or tunnel shows as connected.
guide.help.port.t: Port 7681 is already in use on the phone
guide.help.port.d: Use another local port, for example 8681, and open http://localhost:8681.
guide.help.sleep.t: It stops working after the phone sleeps
guide.help.sleep.d: SSH tunnels close when the app is suspended. Reopen the app and start the tunnel again; Tailscale reconnects by itself.
guide.openvpn.name: OpenVPN Connect
guide.openvpn.blurb: If your company already runs OpenVPN: connect the phone to it, then reach the machine through the VPN.
guide.openvpn.1.t: Connect the phone to the VPN
guide.openvpn.1.d: Install OpenVPN Connect (App Store or Google Play), import the .ovpn profile from your administrator and switch it on. Your phone can now reach the machine’s VPN address, for example 10.8.0.5.
guide.openvpn.2.t: Open an SSH tunnel through the VPN
guide.openvpn.2.d: With the VPN connected, create this tunnel in your SSH app (Termius: Port Forwarding → New Rule · ConnectBot: Edit port forwards · Termux: run the command below). Use the machine’s VPN address, for example 10.8.0.5, as the SSH server:
guide.openvpn.3.n: Opening it through localhost also lets you install it as an app.
guide.openvpn.tip: TERMNEST stays private: it is reachable only through your own SSH login.
guide.ssh.server: Ubuntu server: SSH is usually already running. Use the account you already log in with.
guide.openvpn.2.n: Replace user with the account you normally use to log in to the machine.

cp.lease_help: These are resource register issues, not active locks. An issue may stay open for reuse. Check lease status for the holder and queue; issue age is not lock duration.
cp.cleanup_title: Old records: how to check and close them
cp.cleanup_lease: 1. Resources: run this command from the workspace root on the coordinating machine. A dash in the holder column and an empty queue mean there is no lease to release. The register issue does not need closing.
cp.cleanup_release: If a holder remains, confirm the worker has stopped and the resource is no longer in use. Only the owning task/track session should release it using the command below; replace <task> and <track> with real IDs. Age alone does not authorize releasing another team’s lease.
cp.cleanup_task: 2. Old tasks: open the coordinating session to check MRs, test results, workers and unanswered requests. Once work is complete and closure conditions are met, use set-state <task> closed through the Crew process, then clean up resources. For cancelled work, use the Crew abandon process to preserve branches and commits; do not mark it done just to clear the screen.
cp.cleanup_board: 3. Closed tasks still shown: history is a record for reference. If the GitLab task issue remains open, its owner can sync with announce <task> or board-sweep after checking local state. Hiding an item does not close it. The GitLab connection here only reads data.
cp.closed_record: This task is closed. Track states below are saved records, not active alerts.
cp.old_record: This record has not changed for {0} days. Check with the coordinating session before drawing conclusions or closing it.

ops.crew.title: Crew autopilot 24/7
ops.crew.rule_idle: Idle with open tasks → reminded to continue, once per idle turn, then checked for progress evidence. No quiet hours.
ops.crew.rule_owner: Needs your decision (permission, quota…) → you are told; nothing is answered for you.
ops.crew.rule_blocked: Blocked, session lost or reminded without progress → you are told why.
ops.crew.rule_audit: Every {0} minutes ops-audit inspects each workspace; findings go to Needs you.
ops.crew.rule_source: Status comes from Claude/Codex themselves (the agent's own status file), the process table (workers) and crew (_crew/tasks, _crew/nudge.conf). Missing data is shown as "Unknown", never guessed.
ops.crew.switch_help: On means 24/7. Leaders are found from _crew/nudge.conf on connected machines; no registration needed.
ops.crew.legacy: Using the old configuration ({0} manually registered sessions). Turn the switch on to find teams automatically; old registrations are kept.

ops.crew.no_teams_off: Turn the switch on to find crew leaders on connected machines.
